context.note: Queue task 326, GH#626, stage S5. SECURITY-REVIEWER FAILED commit f09a9d7 on one specific, precise finding: the new INV-174-1 moduledoc text claims GenServer.stop/teardown of the wasmex instance is UNCONDITIONAL on every path (success, exception, timeout) -- this is FALSE against the actual, pre-existing (unmodified by this diff) code. Traced live: (1) module_version_registry.ex's run_call/6 (lines ~431-460) has a pre-existing comment (from REQ-173, not touched by this diff) explicitly documenting that a Wasmex.call_function/4 GenServer.call-timeout exit is deliberately left uncaught by rescue and propagates uncaught -- on that path GenServer.stop(pid) never runs, and the Process.monitor/:DOWN handler (line 641) monitors the TASK pid for ref-counting, not the wasmex instance pid, so it doesn't stop the instance either -- the instance leaks. (2) invoke/4's outer Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) on a Task.yield timeout can also kill the task while it's blocked inside Wasmex.call_function/4, before GenServer.stop(pid) ever runs -- same leak. (3) PluginHandler.run_guest/3 sits under the identical two-layer async_nolink -> Task.yield -> Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) pattern, so the same gap applies there despite this diff's new comment claiming it 'stops the instance unconditionally on every path'. CRITICALLY: SECURITY-REVIEWER confirmed the SUBSTANTIVE isolation property (invocation N+1 never observes invocation N's memory) still genuinely holds -- because a leaked, un-torn-down instance is orphaned and never reused by a later invocation. Isolation comes from 'never sharing a Store' (fresh Store per call, confirmed true), not from 'always torn down' (false as claimed). This is a documentation-accuracy fix only -- no production logic is being changed, since the leak-on-timeout behavior is pre-existing, disclosed (REQ-165/170's own comments already document it), and not a regression this diff introduces.
